def: The set of addresses a component can use and what each one refers to. A PCIe system has several: virtual addresses (software), physical addresses (memory system and root complex), device-visible I/O virtual addresses (devices behind an IOMMU), and configuration space.

Intel's standard register and memory interface for SATA host controllers (2004). One command list of 32 slots per port; completion is discovered by reading host-controller registers. The "before" picture for NVMe.

A register in a PCI/PCIe function's configuration space that tells the system how much address space the function needs and, once programmed, where its registers or memory appear. NVMe controller registers are reached through BAR0.

A communication path carrying data, addresses and control between components. Classic buses (PCI) were shared and parallel; PCIe replaced them with serial point-to-point links but kept the bus-number software model.
Small, fast memory inside the CPU holding copies of recently used main-memory data. DMA must be cache-coherent (by hardware or explicit maintenance) so the CPU and devices see the same data.

A circular buffer of 16-byte completion entries that the NVMe controller writes and the host reads. In NVMe over PCIe it lives in host memory; the host reports consumed entries with the CQ head doorbell.

The part of a device (or host adapter) that understands requests, manages internal resources and reports results. The NVMe controller is the device-side interface the host driver talks to; its outside behavior is specified, its internals are not.
The processor that executes software instructions. A modern CPU package contains several cores, caches, a memory controller and the root complex that connects it to PCIe.
The NVMe controller register at offset 1Ch reporting controller state, including Ready (RDY) and Controller Fatal Status (CFS).

An attribute of the NVMe Dataset Management command (opcode 09h) telling the controller that logical block ranges no longer hold useful data, so the flash translation layer can treat them as stale. Equivalent in purpose to SATA TRIM and SCSI UNMAP.

A small PCIe packet exchanged between the two ends of a link for link-level housekeeping: acknowledgements (Ack/Nak), flow-control credit updates and power management. DLLPs never leave the link they were generated on.

A device reading or writing host memory itself, without the CPU copying the data. On PCIe, DMA writes are Memory Write TLPs from the device and DMA reads are Memory Read TLPs answered by Completions with data.

An NVMe controller register the host writes to announce a new submission queue tail or completion queue head. Doorbells start at offset 1000h, spaced by the stride in CAP.DSTRD; writing one is a posted PCIe Memory Write.
Operating-system software that operates one kind of device and presents it to the rest of the system in a standard way. The Linux nvme driver binds to any PCIe function with the NVMe class code.
How much data can be written to an SSD before it is expected to wear out, quoted as TBW (terabytes written) or DWPD (drive writes per day over the warranty period).

SSD controller firmware that maps logical blocks to physical flash locations, writes out of place, performs garbage collection and wear leveling, and manages spare capacity. Not defined by any NVMe specification.
The FTL process that reclaims flash blocks by copying their remaining valid pages elsewhere and erasing them. It causes write amplification and is the main source of SSD tail latency.
A storage device that records data magnetically on spinning platters read by heads on a moving arm. Random access costs milliseconds (seek plus rotational latency).
A hardware signal that makes a CPU pause, run a handler and resume. PCIe devices use message-signaled interrupts (MSI/MSI-X), which are memory writes the platform converts into interrupts.
Any transfer of information between the CPU-memory core of a computer and the outside world, such as storage, networks and displays. Performed by programmed I/O, polling, or DMA with interrupts.
Hardware that translates device-visible addresses (IOVAs) to physical addresses using per-device tables set up by the operating system, isolating devices from memory they were not given.
Commands completed per second. Meaningful only with block size, access pattern, queue depth and the latency achieved; related to latency by Little's Law.
An address a device uses for DMA when an IOMMU is active. The IOMMU translates it to a physical address; it need not equal the physical address.
One PCIe signal path pair: a differential pair in each direction. Links have 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 lanes; each packet is striped across all lanes of its link.
Time from issuing a request to its completion. Always state where it is measured (device, link, driver, application) and which statistic (median, p99, p99.9).
For a stable system, L = λ × W: average outstanding requests equal throughput times average time in the system. Links queue depth, IOPS and latency.
Device registers made reachable at addresses in the memory address space, so the CPU accesses them with ordinary loads and stores that become PCIe memory transactions.
The PCIe interrupt mechanism in which a device writes a programmed data value to a programmed address for each of up to 2048 vectors. NVMe typically uses one vector per completion queue.
Non-volatile memory storing bits as charge in cells arranged in strings (named after the NOT-AND logic arrangement). Read and programmed in pages, erased in blocks, with limited program/erase cycles.
The SATA feature that lets a drive hold up to 32 outstanding commands in a single queue and complete them out of order.

The storage protocol for non-volatile memory: controllers, namespaces, queues, commands, completions and status, defined by the NVM Express specification set (Base 2.4 and companion command-set and transport specifications in the August 2026 baseline).
Flash capacity reserved for the FTL and not addressable by the host. More over-provisioning lowers write amplification and raises sustained write performance and endurance.
An operating-system data structure mapping virtual pages to physical pages, walked by the CPU's MMU on memory accesses.
The serial, packet-based, point-to-point interconnect between a processor and its devices, defined by the PCI Express Base Specification (PCI-SIG). In this course, the transport that carries NVMe.
The number of commands outstanding at once, either requested by a workload or actually in flight. Higher queue depth lets a parallel device work on more commands simultaneously.
An NVMe submission queue and its associated completion queue, typically one pair per CPU core, each with its own doorbells and interrupt vector.
Main memory: volatile, byte-addressable storage (DRAM in practice) holding programs, data, NVMe queues and DMA buffers.
A small named storage location built into hardware. CPU registers are named by instructions; device registers are reached by address (usually MMIO) and may have side effects when read or written.
The logic, usually inside the CPU package, that connects the CPU and memory to the PCIe hierarchy, originating host requests and receiving device DMA and interrupt messages.
The enterprise serial disk interface carrying SCSI commands, with full-duplex links, dual ports and expanders; drives sit behind a host bus adapter.
The serial disk interface succeeding parallel ATA. Revision 3.x runs at 6 Gb/s (≈ 600 MB/s), with one NCQ queue of 32 commands, typically behind an AHCI host controller.
A storage device built from non-volatile semiconductor memory (NAND flash) and a controller that presents it as logical blocks. Highly parallel internally.
A circular buffer of 64-byte NVMe commands that the host writes and the controller reads. The host announces new entries with the SQ tail doorbell.
The latency of the slowest small fraction of requests (for example p99 or p99.9). In SSDs often dominated by garbage collection and read retries.
Bytes moved per second; equals IOPS multiplied by bytes per command.
The PCIe packet that carries a request (memory, I/O, configuration, message) or a completion between two components.
The mechanism giving each process its own address space, translated page by page to physical memory by the MMU using page tables.
FTL policies that spread program/erase cycles evenly across flash blocks so no block wears out early.
The ratio of bytes programmed to flash to bytes written by the host, caused mainly by garbage-collection copies. 1.0 is ideal.
